newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air China rate cut wins ex-Germany cargo.
newsitem.headline: Air China rate cut wins ex-Germany cargo.

text.p: Air China expects dramatic growth in ex-Germany cargo volumes this autumn following a 10-15 percent rates cut, its German sales agent Penta Shipping GmbH said.
Frank Wortmann, Penta Shipping managing director, said average weekly sales have increased to 28 tonnes in recent weeks from just 10 tonnes a week in January-April this year.
"In October we will have about 50 tonnes a week," he forecast in a Reuters interview.
Wortmann said Air China agreed to cut prices by 10-15 percent on September 1 following poor sales at the start of the year.
Penta Shipping had wanted to cut rates earlier but partner Lufthansa Cargo had not been prepared to go below an agreed minimum level, he added.
Air China flies a weekly Boeing 747-200 freighter from Frankfurt to Beijing and Shanghai and has four weekly passenger flights.
Under a cargo co-operation deal with Lufthansa, Penta is able to sell 35 per cent of total capacity, or about 55 tonnes, and Lufthansa markets the remainder, Wortmann explained.

The Air China weekly freighter was cancelled at least seven times earlier this year since both Penta and Lufthansa were selling at above-market rates and could not generate sufficient volumes, he said.
"The rates cuts has been welcomed by the market and we are now more competitive than before," he said.
"We hope that the rates will remain the same from November and hope then in January to go down again for the weak months," he added.

Wortmann said most cargo from Germany to China is industrial goods, with the bulk heading to Shanghai, while westbound goods are consumer products and textiles. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
